Dorothy lived in the middle of the great Kansas prairies with Uncle Henry and Aunt Em. <break time="0.8s" /> Uncle Henry was a farmer, and Aunt Em was his wife. <break time="0.8s" /> Their house was small because the wood for it had to be carried by wagon many miles. <break time="0.8s" /> It had four walls, a floor, and a roof, which made one room. <break time="0.8s" /> In this room there were a rusty cookstove, a cupboard for the dishes, a table, and some chairs. <break time="0.8s" /> Uncle Henry and Aunt Em had a big bed in one corner, and Dorothy had a little bed in another. <break time="0.8s" /> Under the floor there was a small, dark hole that the family called a cyclone cellar. <break time="0.8s" /> The family could go there when one of those great whirlwinds came. <break time="0.8s" /> A trap door in the middle of the floor led down to it. <break time="0.8s" /> When Dorothy stood in the doorway, she could see nothing but the great gray prairie. <break time="0.8s" /> The sun had baked the plowed land into a gray mass with little cracks. <break time="0.8s" /> Once the house had been painted, but now it was as dull and gray as everything else.

도로시는 살았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 캔자스의 넓은 대평원 한가운데에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 헨리 아저씨, 엠 아주머니와 함께. <break time="0.8s" /> 헨리 아저씨는 농부였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 엠 아주머니는 그의 아내였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그들의 집은 작았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 집을 지을 나무를. <break time="0.8s" /> 마차로 실어 와야 했기 때문이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 몇 마일이나 되는 먼 길을. <break time="0.8s" /> 집에는 벽 네 개, 바닥, 지붕이 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것들이 방 하나를 이루었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 이 방에는 있었다 녹슨 요리용 난로. <break time="0.8s" /> 접시를 넣는 찬장. <break time="0.8s" /> 식탁 하나, 그리고 의자 몇 개가. <break time="0.8s" /> 헨리 아저씨와 엠 아주머니에게는 큰 침대가 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 한쪽 구석에. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 도로시에게는 작은 침대가 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 다른 구석에. <break time="0.8s" /> 바닥 아래에는. <break time="0.8s" /> 작고 어두운 구멍이 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 가족은 그것을 회오리바람 지하실이라고 불렀다. <break time="0.8s" /> 가족은 그곳으로 갈 수 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그런 거대한 회오리바람이 불어올 때. <break time="0.8s" /> 방바닥 한가운데에 있는 들창문이. <break time="0.8s" /> 아래로 그곳까지 이어져 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 도로시가 문간에 서면. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀에게 보이는 것은 오직 넓은 회색 대평원뿐이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 햇볕이 갈아 놓은 땅을 구웠다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 회색 덩어리로 만들었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 여기저기 작은 틈이 갈라진. <break time="0.8s" /> 한때 집에는 페인트가 칠해져 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 이제 집은 칙칙한 회색이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 다른 모든 것과 똑같이.

When Aunt Em came there to live. <break time="0.8s" /> She was a young, pretty wife. <break time="0.8s" /> But the sun and wind. <break time="0.8s" /> Had changed her, too. <break time="0.8s" /> They had taken the sparkle. <break time="0.8s" /> From her eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> And left them a sober gray. <break time="0.8s" /> She was thin and pale now. <break time="0.8s" /> And she never smiled. <break time="0.8s" /> When Dorothy. <break time="0.8s" /> Who was an orphan. <break time="0.8s" /> First came to her. <break time="0.8s" /> The childs laughter. <break time="0.8s" /> Startled Aunt Em. <break time="0.8s" /> Aunt Em would scream. <break time="0.8s" /> And press her hand on her heart. <break time="0.8s" /> Whenever she heard. <break time="0.8s" /> The girls merry voice. <break time="0.8s" /> She still looked at Dorothy. <break time="0.8s" /> And wondered. <break time="0.8s" /> How the girl could find. <break time="0.8s" /> Anything to laugh at. <break time="0.8s" /> Uncle Henry never laughed. <break time="0.8s" /> For he worked hard. <break time="0.8s" /> From morning till night. <break time="0.8s" /> He was gray. <break time="0.8s" /> From his long beard. <break time="0.8s" /> To his rough boots. <break time="0.8s" /> And he rarely spoke. <break time="0.8s" /> It was Toto. <break time="0.8s" /> That made Dorothy laugh. <break time="0.8s" /> And saved her. <break time="0.8s" /> From growing as gray as everything else. <break time="0.8s" /> Toto was a little black dog. <break time="0.8s" /> With long, silky hair. <break time="0.8s" /> And small black eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> That twinkled merrily. <break time="0.8s" /> Toto played all day long. <break time="0.8s" /> And Dorothy played with him. <break time="0.8s" /> And loved him dearly.

When Aunt Em came there to live, she was a young, pretty wife. <break time="0.8s" /> But the sun and wind had changed her, too. <break time="0.8s" /> They had taken the sparkle from her eyes and left them a sober gray. <break time="0.8s" /> She was thin and pale now, and she never smiled. <break time="0.8s" /> When Dorothy, who was an orphan, first came to her, the childs laughter startled Aunt Em. <break time="0.8s" /> Aunt Em would scream and press her hand on her heart whenever she heard the girls merry voice. <break time="0.8s" /> She still looked at Dorothy and wondered how the girl could find anything to laugh at. <break time="0.8s" /> Uncle Henry never laughed, for he worked hard from morning till night. <break time="0.8s" /> He was gray from his long beard to his rough boots, and he rarely spoke. <break time="0.8s" /> It was Toto that made Dorothy laugh and saved her from growing as gray as everything else. <break time="0.8s" /> Toto was a little black dog with long, silky hair and small black eyes that twinkled merrily. <break time="0.8s" /> Toto played all day long, and Dorothy played with him and loved him dearly.

엠 아주머니가 그곳에 살러 왔을 때. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀는 젊고 예쁜 아내였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 햇볕과 바람이. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀도 바꾸어 놓았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것들은 반짝임을 빼앗았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀의 눈에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 눈을 칙칙한 회색으로 남겨 두었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 이제 그녀는 마르고 창백했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 전혀 웃지 않았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 도로시가. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 아이는 고아였는데. <break time="0.8s" /> 처음 그녀에게 왔을 때. <break time="0.8s" /> 아이의 웃음소리가. <break time="0.8s" /> 엠 아주머니를 깜짝 놀라게 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 엠 아주머니는 비명을 지르곤 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 손으로 가슴을 눌렀다. <break time="0.8s" /> 들을 때마다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 아이의 명랑한 목소리를. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀는 여전히 도로시를 바라보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 궁금해했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 아이가 어떻게 찾아낼 수 있는지. <break time="0.8s" /> 웃을 거리를. <break time="0.8s" /> 헨리 아저씨는 전혀 웃지 않았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 고되게 일했기 때문이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 아침부터 밤까지. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 회색이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 긴 턱수염부터. <break time="0.8s" /> 거친 장화까지. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 말을 거의 하지 않았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 바로 토토였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 도로시를 웃게 한 것은. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그녀를 지켜 준 것도. <break time="0.8s" /> 다른 모든 것처럼 회색이 되지 않도록. <break time="0.8s" /> 토토는 작은 검은 개였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 길고 비단 같은 털이 있는. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 작고 까만 두 눈. <break time="0.8s" /> 즐겁게 반짝이는. <break time="0.8s" /> 토토는 하루 종일 놀았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 도로시는 토토와 함께 놀았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 토토를 무척 사랑했다.

Today, however. <break time="0.8s" /> Dorothy and Toto were not playing. <break time="0.8s" /> Uncle Henry sat on the doorstep. <break time="0.8s" /> And looked worriedly at the sky. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was even grayer than usual. <break time="0.8s" /> Dorothy stood in the door. <break time="0.8s" /> With Toto in her arms. <break time="0.8s" /> And looked at the sky, too. <break time="0.8s" /> From the far north. <break time="0.8s" /> Came a low wail of the wind. <break time="0.8s" /> And the long grass. <break time="0.8s" /> Bowed in waves. <break time="0.8s" /> Then they heard. <break time="0.8s" /> A sharp whistling in the air. <break time="0.8s" /> From the south. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly Uncle Henry stood up. <break time="0.8s" /> And called to his wife. <break time="0.8s" /> There is a cyclone coming, Em. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he ran. <break time="0.8s" /> Toward the sheds. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the cows and horses were kept. <break time="0.8s" /> Aunt Em dropped her work. <break time="0.8s" /> And came to the door. <break time="0.8s" /> One look told her. <break time="0.8s" /> That the danger was very close. <break time="0.8s" /> Quick, Dorothy. <break time="0.8s" /> She screamed. <break time="0.8s" /> Run for the cellar.

하지만 오늘은. <break time="0.8s" /> 도로시와 토토가 놀고 있지 않았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 헨리 아저씨는 문간 계단에 앉았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 걱정스럽게 하늘을 보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하늘은 여느 때보다 훨씬 더 잿빛이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 도로시는 문에 서 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 토토를 품에 안고. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그녀도 하늘을 보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 먼 북쪽에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 낮게 우는 듯한 바람 소리가 들려왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 긴 풀들이. <break time="0.8s" /> 물결치듯 고개를 숙였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그때 그들은 들었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 공중을 가르는 날카로운 휘파람 소리를. <break time="0.8s" /> 남쪽에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 갑자기 헨리 아저씨가 일어났다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 아내에게 소리쳤다. <break time="0.8s" /> 회오리바람이 오고 있어, 엠. <break time="0.8s" /> 그러고는 그는 달려갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 헛간 쪽으로. <break time="0.8s" /> 소와 말을 두는. <break time="0.8s" /> 엠 아주머니는 하던 일을 내려놓았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 문으로 왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 한 번 보자 그녀는 알 수 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 위험이 아주 가까이 왔다는 것을. <break time="0.8s" /> 빨리, 도로시. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀가 소리쳤다. <break time="0.8s" /> 지하실로 뛰어.

Just then. <break time="0.8s" /> Toto jumped out of Dorothys arms. <break time="0.8s" /> And hid under the bed. <break time="0.8s" /> While the girl tried to get him. <break time="0.8s" /> Aunt Em threw open the trap door. <break time="0.8s" /> Badly frightened. <break time="0.8s" /> She climbed down the ladder. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the small, dark hole. <break time="0.8s" /> At last Dorothy caught Toto. <break time="0.8s" /> And started to follow her aunt. <break time="0.8s" /> When she was halfway across the room. <break time="0.8s" /> There came a great shriek. <break time="0.8s" /> From the wind. <break time="0.8s" /> The house shook so hard. <break time="0.8s" /> That she lost her footing. <break time="0.8s" /> And sat down suddenly on the floor. <break time="0.8s" /> Then a strange thing happened. <break time="0.8s" /> The house whirled around. <break time="0.8s" /> Two or three times. <break time="0.8s" /> And rose slowly through the air. <break time="0.8s" /> The north wind and the south wind. <break time="0.8s" /> Met at the very place. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the house stood. <break time="0.8s" /> That place became. <break time="0.8s" /> The exact center of the cyclone. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the air is usually still. <break time="0.8s" /> But the strong wind on every side. <break time="0.8s" /> Pushed the house higher and higher. <break time="0.8s" /> At the very top of the cyclone. <break time="0.8s" /> It was carried. <break time="0.8s" /> Miles and miles away. <break time="0.8s" /> As easily as a feather.
